about.title: Belvedere Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Belvedere is a small, close-knit community tucked along the Tiburon Peninsula in Marin County, and its workforce spans everything from waterfront maintenance and marina operations to contracting work on the hillside homes near Beach Road and Peninsula Road. When a work injury happens here, most people assume workers' compensation is the only path forward — and in many cases, it is the required first step. But California law also allows a separate claim against a negligent third party, such as an equipment manufacturer, a subcontractor, or a property owner who isn't your direct employer. Sorting out which path applies, and whether both might be available, takes a careful look at how the injury happened. Our team can review the details of your situation and explain what options may exist under California law.

items.title: Third-Party Claims Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: California generally treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be held responsible. We can help determine if a separate claim applies to your situation.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California law generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate a claim. Our team can walk you through what documentation and timing matter most.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about how reporting might affect your job, we can explain your rights before you act.

items.question: I work for a small business in Belvedere — does workers' comp still apply?
items.answer: In most cases, yes, California requires nearly all employers to carry workers' compensation coverage regardless of size. We can confirm your employer's coverage status and help you understand next steps.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly if I'm hurt on the job?
items.answer: Generally, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, meaning a direct lawsuit is usually not an option regardless of fault. However, if a third party — like a contractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer — contributed to your injury, a separate claim against them may be possible.

items.question: What if my injury happened near Beach Road or Peninsula Road while doing work errands?
items.answer: If you were injured while performing job duties on Belvedere's roads, such as making deliveries or traveling between work sites, it may still fall under workers' comp, and a third party like another driver could also bear responsibility. We can look at where and how the injury occurred to sort out which claims may apply.

items.question: Is there a deadline for filing a third-party claim?
items.answer: Yes, third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year statute of limitations. Waiting too long can limit your options, so it helps to talk with us sooner rather than later.
